proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(R_{C,c}(z)=W_{C,c}(z)-\mu_z\) and
\[
b_{C,c,k}=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}R_{C,c}(z).
\]
Under either design in the statement, assignments are independent across clusters, a slice-\(k\) hit has probability \(r_{C,k}\), and the assignment conditional on a hit is uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\).  For the Bernoulli-label design the last assertion follows from exchangeability of the \(n_0\) unit assignments conditional on their treated count.  Hence
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
 \frac{\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}R_{C,c}(Z_c)}{r_{C,k}}
\right]=b_{C,c,k}.
\]
The definition of \(\widehat U_C\) now gives
\[
\mathbb E(\widehat U_{C,k})
=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\mu_z+C^{-1}\sum_{c=1}^Cb_{C,c,k}
=U_{C,k}.
\]
Only assignment is random here, by Assumption~\(\texttt{ass:assignment-only-randomness}\).

Define the centered cluster vector
\[
X_{C,c,k}=
\frac{\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}R_{C,c}(Z_c)}{r_{C,k}}-b_{C,c,k}.
\]
Because distinct slices are disjoint, direct multiplication yields
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(X_{C,c,i},X_{C,c,j})=
\begin{cases}
r_{C,k}^{-1}M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}R_{C,c}(z)^2-b_{C,c,k}^2,
 &i=j=k,\\
-b_{C,c,i}b_{C,c,j},&i\ne j.
\end{cases}
\tag{1}
\]
Also
\(\sqrt C(\widehat U_C-U_C)=C^{-1/2}\sum_cX_{C,c}\).

Let \(t_{C,c}(z)=W_{C,c}(z)\) and
\(\lambda_C=C^{-1}\sum_c\delta_{t_{C,c}}\).  Since \(T\) is finite, every subsequence has a further subsequence with \(\lambda_C\to\lambda\).  Assumption~\(\texttt{ass:cell-margin-convergence}\) gives
\[
\sum_{t:t(z)=w}\lambda_t=f_{z,w}.
\]
The definition of \(\mu_z\), followed by Assumption~\(\texttt{ass:common-welfare-tie}\), gives
\(\sum_t\lambda_tu_k(t)=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\mu_z=\mu_0\).
Thus \(\lambda\in\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\).  Averaging (1), using \(r_C\to r\), and applying the definitions of \(A\), \(g\), and \(\Xi\), gives
\[
C^{-1}\sum_c\operatorname{Cov}(X_{C,c})
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{diag}\{A_k(\lambda)/r_k\}_{k=1}^K-\Xi(\lambda)
=\Sigma(r,\lambda).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus no subsequential covariance is outside \(\mathfrak S(r;f,\mu_0)\).

Conversely, fix \(\lambda\in\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\).  Choose integer counts \(N_{C,t}\) summing to \(C\) with \(N_{C,t}/C\to\lambda_t\), by rounding finitely many \(C\lambda_t\)'s and assigning the residual to one type.  For every occurrence of \(t\), realize \(t(z)\in Wgrid\) by setting exactly \(n_0t(z)\) unit outcomes equal to one at assignment \(z\).  This is permitted by unrestricted binary interference.  The empirical type law tends to \(\lambda\), so its cell margins tend to \(f\), its limiting slice means equal \(\mu_0\), and (2) tends to \(\Sigma(r,\lambda)\).  This proves attainability.

For fixed \(r\) and \(Dtest\), expansion of \(A\) and \(\Xi\) makes
\(\operatorname{tr}\{Dtest\,\Sigma(r,\lambda)\}\) affine in the finitely many \(\lambda_t\)'s.  The definition of \(\Lambda\) imposes finitely many linear equalities and nonnegativity constraints; compactness gives both extrema.  With rational \(f,r,Dtest\), all coefficients are rational.  A primal feasible vector and dual feasible vector with the same rational objective certify optimality by
\[
c^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le y^{\mathsf T}b
\quad\text{when}\quad
A\lambda=b,\ \lambda\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c.
\]
Finite Gaussian elimination and pivoting yield rational optimal basic primal and dual solutions.  This proves the final certificate claim.

In the balanced instance each target cell is Bernoulli on \(\{0,1\}\) with mean \(1/2\).  Let \(X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).  Set every coordinate in \(\mathcal S_1\cup\mathcal S_2\) equal to \(X\), or set the coordinates in \(\mathcal S_1\) equal to \(X\) and those in \(\mathcal S_2\) equal to \(1-X\); complete all other slices identically.  Both couplings lie in \(\Lambda(f,1/2)\).  They give respectively
\[
(g_1,g_2)=(X-1/2,X-1/2),
\qquad
(g_1,g_2)=(X-1/2,1/2-X).
\]
Thus \(A_1=A_2=1/4\), both relevant diagonal entries of \(\Xi\) are \(1/4\), and \(\Xi_{12}\) is respectively \(1/4\) and \(-1/4\).  The definition of \(\Sigma\) gives common first two diagonal entries and off-diagonal entries \(-1/4\) and \(1/4\).  Their difference has a \(2\)-by-\(2\) principal block with zero diagonal and nonzero off-diagonal, so it is indefinite; neither matrix dominates the other.

Incomparability alone is not enough for the last assertion, so we prove it separately.  Write \(d_k=1/(4r_k)\).  Since \(M_2=M_3=15\), every realized \(g_k\), \(k=2,3\), is an odd multiple of \(1/30\).  Hence \(\Xi_{kk}\ge1/900\), with equality attained by mixing a seven-one configuration on the slice and its complement.  Therefore
\[
\sup_{\Omega\in\mathfrak S}e_k^{\mathsf T}\Omega e_k=d_k-1/900,\qquad k=2,3.
\tag{3}
\]
Constant-within-slice couplings attain \(g_2=g_3\) and \(g_2=-g_3\), respectively.  Since \(\Xi\) is positive semidefinite, these zero contrast squares are minimal, and
\[
\sup_{\Omega\in\mathfrak S}(e_2\pm e_3)^{\mathsf T}\Omega(e_2\pm e_3)=d_2+d_3.
\tag{4}
\]
If a symmetric \(Q\) represented all directional supports, (3) would give
\(Q_{22}=d_2-1/900\) and \(Q_{33}=d_3-1/900\).  The plus case in (4) would force \(Q_{23}=1/900\), while the minus case would force \(Q_{23}=-1/900\), a contradiction.  Thus no such \(Q\), and in particular no such dominating \(Q\), exists.

By Theorem~\(\texttt{thm:sharp-covariance-set}\), \(\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\) is a nonempty compact polytope and has finitely many vertices.  For \(i<j\) and a vertex \(\lambda\), define
\[
\phi_{ij,\lambda}(r)=
\frac{A_i(\lambda)}{r_i}+\frac{A_j(\lambda)}{r_j}
-(e_i-e_j)^{\mathsf T}\Xi(\lambda)(e_i-e_j).
\]
The maximum of the linear objective in \(\lambda\) occurs at a vertex, so
\[
H(r;f)=\max_{i<j}\max_{\lambda\in\operatorname{vert}(\Lambda)}
\phi_{ij,\lambda}(r).
\tag{5}
\]
Every \(A_k(\lambda)\ge0\); hence each \(\phi\) is convex on the positive orthant, and so is their finite maximum.  The set \(\Delta_K(\rho)\) is nonempty and compact because \(0<\rho<1/K\), proving exact-count attainment.  Every entry of \(B\) is positive because all \(m_k\)'s are interior counts.  Hence \(Bp\) remains uniformly positive on the compact simplex, proving nominal-label attainment by continuity.

For an active scenario,
\[
[\nabla\phi_{ij,\lambda}(r)]_k
=-\frac{A_k(\lambda)}{r_k^2}\mathbf1\{k\in\{i,j\}\}.
\tag{6}
\]
The directional derivative of the finite maximum (5) is the maximum of the active directional derivatives.  Finite-dimensional separation therefore gives the necessary-and-sufficient condition
\[
0\in
\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla\phi_{ij,\lambda}(r):(i,j,\lambda)\text{ active}\}
+N_{\Delta_K(\rho)}(r).
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed, (7) makes every feasible directional derivative nonnegative and convexity gives global optimality; if (7) fails, strict separation supplies a feasible descent direction.  Eliminating affine dependencies expresses the convex-hull element using at most \(K+1\) active gradients.  This is the asserted weighted stationarity equation and simplex normal.  For the nominal problem, the identical argument applies to the active gradients
\(B^{\mathsf T}\nabla\phi_{ij,\lambda}(Bp)\) and the normal cone of \(\Delta_K\).

Each active vertex is certified by its primal feasibility and an LP dual vector with equal objective, using weak duality from the preceding theorem.  Activity, those finitely many LP certificates, the nonnegative weights summing to one, and the normal multipliers form the stated finite certificate.  Conversely they imply (7), proving global optimality.

Let
\[
E_C=\sqrt C(\widehat U_C-U_C),\qquad
h_C=\sqrt C(U_C-\mu_0\mathbf1_K).
\]
Theorem~\(\texttt{thm:sharp-covariance-set}\) gives, on a further subsequence, a \(\lambda\in\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\) for which the covariance of \(E_C\) tends to \(\Sigma(r,\lambda)\).  For fixed \(a\in\mathbb R^K\), \(a^{\mathsf T}E_C\) is a sum of independent centered cluster contributions.  The positive limiting hit rates bound inverse probabilities, and \(0\le W\le1\) bounds every unnormalized contribution.  Thus each normalized summand is \(O(C^{-1/2})\), so the Lindeberg remainder is eventually zero.  Taylor expansion of its characteristic function has a total third-order remainder \(O(C^{-1/2})\), and multiplication of the factors gives
\[
a^{\mathsf T}E_C\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(r,\lambda)a).
\]
This also holds at zero variance.  Applying the identity for every \(a\) proves by Cramér--Wold that
\[
E_C\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma(r,\lambda)).
\tag{8}
\]
This derives, rather than assumes, the limit law from independence, positivity, bounded outcomes, and the stated Lindeberg condition.

Assumption~\(\texttt{ass:local-welfare-array}\) gives \(h_C\to h\), and the empirical-best selector acts on \(h_C+E_C\).  Pass to a further subsequence on which the least maximizer \(i_C\) of \(h_C\) is constant, equal to \(i\).  Then \(i\) maximizes \(h\).  Put \(d_{ij}=h_i-h_j\ge0\).  If \(j\ne i\) is selected, then
\(h_{C,j}+E_{C,j}\ge h_{C,i}+E_{C,i}\).  The scaled loss is bounded by the range of \(h_C\), hence is uniformly bounded.  From (8), one-dimensional contrast convergence, and \(h_C\to h\),
\[
\limsup_C\sqrt C\,\mathbb E[
\max_kU_{C,k}-U_{C,\delta_{\mathrm{EB}}(\widehat U_C)}]
\le
\sum_{j\ne i}d_{ij}
\Phi\!\left(-\frac{d_{ij}}{\sqrt{V_{ij}(r,\lambda)}}\right),
\tag{9}
\]
where a term is zero if \(d_{ij}=0\) or \(V_{ij}=0\).  The zero-variance case follows because the limiting contrast is then the negative constant \(-d_{ij}\).

By the definition of \(\kappa\), each term in (9) is at most
\(\kappa\sqrt{V_{ij}(r,\lambda)}\), and every such variance is at most \(H(r;f)\).  Therefore
\[
\limsup_C\sqrt C\,\mathbb E[
\max_kU_{C,k}-U_{C,\delta_{\mathrm{EB}}(\widehat U_C)}]
\le\kappa(K-1)\sqrt{H(r;f)}.
\]
Uniformity over \(h\) in a compact set follows by contradiction: a violating sequence has a convergent \(h\)-subsequence and then, by finiteness of \(T\), a compatible-coupling subsequence to which the argument applies.  Finite-\(C\) regret is bounded by one because every \(U_{C,k}\in[0,1]\).  Finally, the definition of \(rStar,pStar\) and Theorem~\(\texttt{thm:robust-design-kkt}\) minimize \(H\) on the two domains, and the displayed bound is increasing in \(H\).

Here \(M_2={6\choose2}=15={6\choose4}=M_3\).  Every target-cell marginal is Bernoulli on \(\{0,1\}\) with mean \(1/2\), so for \(k=2,3\),
\[
A_k(\lambda)=\frac1{15}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}
\mathbb E_\lambda(t(z)-1/2)^2=1/4.
\]
For each type, the sum of fifteen numbers from \(\{-1/2,1/2\}\) is a nonzero odd multiple of \(1/2\).  Hence
\[
|g_k(t)|\ge1/30,\qquad
\Xi_{kk}(\lambda)=\mathbb E_\lambda g_k(t)^2\ge1/900.
\]
Substitution into \(\Sigma_{kk}=A_k/r_k-\Xi_{kk}\) gives
\(\Sigma_{kk}(r,\lambda)\le1/(4r_k)-1/900\), excluding the stated endpoint.

On the retained face, constancy within a slice gives variables \(X_i,X_j\in Wgrid\) with \(t(z)=X_k\) for \(z\in\mathcal S_k\).  The constraints defining \(\Lambda\) reduce to the prescribed marginal laws of \(X_i\) and \(X_j\), and their only joint covariance term is
\(\mathbb E[(X_i-\mu_i)(X_j-\mu_j)]\).  Thus the support LP is precisely the finite transportation program over masses \(\gamma_{ab}\ge0\) with prescribed row and column sums.

Order both supports increasingly.  If positive mass occurs at crossed cells \((a,d)\) and \((b,c)\), where \(a<b\) and \(c<d\), moving an amount \(\varepsilon\) from those cells to \((a,c)\) and \((b,d)\) preserves the marginals and changes \(\mathbb E(X_iX_j)\) by
\[
\varepsilon(b-a)(d-c)\ge0.
\]
Compactness gives an optimizer; choosing an optimizer that lexicographically maximizes northwest cumulative masses and applying this exchange rules out crossings, yielding the comonotone quantile coupling.  Reversing the second order yields the countermonotone coupling.  These are the discrete Fréchet--Hoeffding upper and lower covariance bounds, proving the reduction.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A terminating finite rational algorithm that gives outward brackets, all-minimizer cells, and selector and covariance witnesses for both nested exact-regret design problems.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen receipt handle specifies a search architecture but no verified uniform approximation theorem for the all-Borel Gaussian selector game.  In particular, the quantitatively uniform finite-prior lower transfer, enlarged-cell selector upper transfer, and one computable diagonal schedule are absent; moreover the arbitrary frozen marginal table has no declared finite effective encoding.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced covariance support to certified finite linear programs; checked compact positive-rate design regions, finite Gaussian priors, rectangle selectors, inverse-CDF Borel decoding, boundary pruning, and LAN transfer as the natural route.  The presolve draft itself records that the constants and common diagonal schedule have not been verified end to end.
open_obligations.partial_result: For rational \(f\), \(r\), and a rational support direction, every covariance support value is already a rational linear-program optimum with finite primal and dual certificates.  This does not certify the nonlinear all-Borel-selector value \(G\), uniformly over covariance and design, or its optimization.  The presolve architecture supplies boundary pruning, finite Gaussian prior and selector approximations, and Borel inverse-CDF decoding, but its own audit leaves unproved the quantitatively uniform finite-prior lower transfer, enlarged-cell selector upper transfer, and a single computable diagonal refinement schedule.  Therefore the terminating outward-bracket theorem does not yet follow from the frozen primitives.
